Magcore computation. It was a transistor-less electrical computer. It would have never scaled down though. It's still cool that you can build a computer out of classical electrical components. It would be useful in an apocalypse if you can't dope silicon wafers.

It's like magcore memory but with gates. It requires a special coil core with hysteresis.

Transistors are electronic components which use one electrical current to switch another one on and off. This might not sound like much, but it's the basic building block needed for computer logic and every processor you've ever owned boils down to millions of tiny transistors on a tiny silicon wafer. The circuits are formed by creating areas of silicon which have high concentrations of either boron or potassium (doping).

Mag core is short for magnetic core memory. It was a type of permanent storage used back in the 60s which involved thousands of absolutely tiny electromagnets. They had to be made by hand and the act of reading them also erased them, but they were extremely fast and disc drives hadn't been invented yet, let alone optical media.

So making a computer with no transistors and mag core memory is a bit like hand-crafting a B-52 out of mahogany and running it on a steam engine. Completely useless, utterly ridiculous, but extremely hard-core.
